This Match-3 strategy game with visual novel, role-playing game (RPG) elements and adult content by KAGAMI WORKs and Paradise Project features 8 different short stories (An additional 4 with DLC) that are viewed through a magic mirror. Starting with the dark elf Daisy, a different monster or character will fight the female character to the ending of each story arc. The story revolves around these characters:

[b]Daisy[/b]: A dark elf who steals from the rich to give to the poor.
[b]Yoko[/b]: An archer and priestess of a shrine in Kyoto and defends the city from monsters.
[b]Cai Yun[/b]: A Chinese zombie who lies sealed inside a cave and awaits the return of the next reincarnation of her former lover and fellow disciple.
[b]Lin[/b]: An ice dragon who serves a family of dragon knights as the family's maid. 
[b]Unita[/b]: An orc she-warrior who has to hunt and slay a ferocious monster to be recognized as a warrior in her tribe.
[b]Ketsuno Ana[/b]: A shogun girl from ancient Japan who somehow ended up at a modern Comincon (anime exhibition for otakus) and was mistaken for a cosplayer. 
[b]Ebony (Augie Terry)[/b]: A queen of the Empire of Yellow Sand with grand ambitions to attain divinity at all costs.
[b]Martha[/b]: A nun who works at a convent to distribute food to the needy and spread her god's message.

Having spent 21 hours to reach all endings and obtain all achievements in this game, the storyline in this game can be controversial with multiple instances of BDSM, sexual assault and physical torture. Here is where I will mention a warning to all readers that if these controversial themes feel uncomfortable, look elsewhere, otherwise read on.

[u]Plot and character backgrounds[/u]

Despite the controversial, dark and adult subject matter among the short stories in this game, I would still praise the scriptwriter for having the imagination to come up with eight different short stories that  are different from the usual fare in a fantasy or romance story. They do this by combining both genres to tell 8 different stories of lost romance where 8 different characters or monsters might feel compelled to punish each girl towards a pain route and ending, or to excite the girl towards a pleasure route and ending after having to fight each girl across 3 different Match-3 stages. Although most of them have selfish and unsavoury motives on each girl, they also have an additional layer of complexity to describe and spur that motivation. A few of the characters are more wholesome yet they are forced due to circumstances to act in that way which also adds to the complexity of such a romance. This results in excellent storytelling which not many short stories have. After a few patch updates in November 2017 and September 2018, the game has fewer errors in the English version.

[u]Artwork[/u]

The artwork in this game is excellent by being attractive and colourful. The CGs use a large variety of different colours while each female character has animated sprites with different facial expressions and blinking eyes as the player does battle with them during the Match-3 and Tame segments of the game. The opening theme will show various CGs, background scenes, the cast of characters and character voice list with great animation throughout. The game also has great artwork in the game cover, Steam achievement icons, badges, emoticons and profile backgrounds. For those who prefer to uncensor the game and remove the flowers and SakuraGame rabbit in the Steam version of this game, a patch for this game is available by searching through the game's discussion boards, some reviews or from certain Steam groups. The Cosplay DLC has an additional 219 photos of female cosplayers featuring all 12 girls from all short stories.

[u]Voice acting and background music[/u]

Having voice acting by at least 5 different voice actresses for each female character in both the visual novel and Match-3 segment of this game serve to highlight, bring out and make this game more interesting. The background music (BGM) are great by matching the setting of the game and the character personality of each Match-3 opponent. My favourite soundtracks in this game are Lost Romance which begin by being pleasant and become stirring during the chorus. Although this BGM is played throughout in the game's title screen, menu options and visual novel segments, it remains as one of my personal favourite soundtracks and I still listen to it despite playing the game for 18 hours. The oriental BGM for Yoko's and Cai Yun's stages, the stirring BGM for Daisy's stages and the song with vocals Mirror that is in the opening theme and soundtrack DLC are also among my favourite soundtracks in this game.

[u]Gameplay[/u]

The Match-3 gameplay is the main highlight of this game although if this game is a pure visual novel, I also wouldn't mind paying 2-4 dollars for the 12 short stories alone. As a Match-3 strategy game where the player has to reduce the opponent's health to zero, the game rewards players who build longer chains to deal more damage to an opponent, gain more health or rage or to create a super gem that can create a very large special effect depending on chosen skill and award more money at the end of the match. Each opponent has a different set of strengths and special abilities where some may need certain skills and items to counter their strengths and special moves. Each girl will also say something that is voiced in Japanese whenever they use a special ability, take damage and have their clothes torn or broken, win or lose at the end of the stage.

The achievements are more or less reasonable where although there are a few achievements that rely on luck, most of them can be obtained after a number of attempts. For those who are looking for a more challenging set of Match-3 stages, the game also has an unlockable challenge mode that is unlocked after reaching an ending with Martha as the final female character. This mode is entirely optional and is something like an ironman mode where the player will have to make decisions on which skills and items to equip, adjust skills accordingly, earn hearts after winning each round to purchase a replacement item for a spent item slot and the player is assigned a rank score at the end of the game. All these help to make the game fun and replayable without being too difficult or excessively grindy.

The Tame segment gameplay is the most controversial part of this game with heavy NSFW content which may make players uncomfortable where it involves choosing which body part or item to apply to certain parts on the captured girl's body. I feel this game wouldn't have raised as much controversy without this segment, which doesn't add anything much to the game other than adult content and those who want to get all achievements have to refer to published community guides or experiment with different combinations in this adult segment.

Overall, this Match-3 strategy game with 8 different short stories is recommended only for adult players who like the Match-3 gameplay and fantasy visual novel segment that have compelling storyline, great artwork, voice acting and background music. If you don't mind the heavy NSFW content and controversial content in this game, it is highly recommended to get this game with the soundtrack and Lost Shards DLC (Included in full review at link below).

This was a pleasant surprise. For its absurdly low cost, I was expecting a lame, throwaway collection of porn pictures tied together with some token, basic match-three puzzle gameplay to give it the barest claim to being a "game". What I actually got was a solid, enjoyable battle puzzle game which told a collection of surprisingly engaging short stories, leading up to some very fap-worthy porn.

I found the match-three gameplay surprisingly fun. Rather than just racing against time to fill a bar, you're in combat against the story's girl who's fighting back, forcing you to keep an eye on your HP and fight off the effects of her special attacks as you wear down her own HP. What really makes the gameplay is the customisation- the ability to choose what skills and items you bring into the battle with you. Each girl has a different battle style that makes them feel quite different from each other- Daisy is very fast, taking far more actions than other girls, Ketsuno Ana has incredibly high defence, forcing you to break her armour to have a chance of beating her in time, Martha deals almost no damage to you, but constantly heals herself. As a puzzle game, I found myself actively enjoying it for more than just the girly eye candy. As an added bonus, there's a survival rush mode unlocked after you finish the story of every girl in the main game where you beat as many girls as you can in a row while earning more currency to buy consumable items mid-battle. While a bit token, it's a good way to earn more money to buy some of the more expensive upgrades (especially the level 4 and 5 stat upgrades).

The stories were also far better than I expected. Rather than the mess of engrish I'd been expecting, the translation was pretty good and easy to understand. Sometimes the story can be a bit odd or even unpleasant, but they're still quite engaging, and some are actually surprisingly moving. Every girl has two possible endings and while they're usually as simple as "good end, bad end", there's a lot more nuance to some of them- Ketsuno Ana's good end is "happy" but rather shallow, but her bad end actually brings some serious feels. There are also VN choices you make once at each story stage, but these are token- a "right" and "wrong" choice which either buffs or penalises the girl in the next fight, and doesn't affect the story beyond some altered dialogue.

I should also take this moment to recommend the "Lost Shards" DLC. The four extra girl stories you get in there are arguably the best ones in the game- the stories are longer and I think better-written with some surprising plot twists and really intense emotional story beats. Additionally, the ero scenes are better, with a proper penetration sequence adding some extra interactive gameplay. However the translation quality of them has slipped a bit compared to the base game- as well as some clunkier sentence phrasing, a few things have just been flat-out mistranslated (Mafercca is repeatedly called a "succubus" when it should be "witch"). Still, if you're going to get the game at all, get the DLC as well.

Then there's the ero. Apart from the ability to blow the girls' clothes off during the battles, there's an interactive sex scene at the climax of their story. Your actions determine which end you get, and while these are just foreplay, most of the girls have an additional scene in some of their endings. As mentioned, the DLC girls get an extra scene where you get to actually have sex with them, which makes them better, but the mouse control here is finnicky. There's also a free replay mode unlocked after you've beaten a girl's bonus stage which is OK to dabble with. You're definitely buying this game for the porn, but it's arguably one of the weaker aspects- nice to look at and listen to, but a bit weak gameplay-wise. Then again, you get your gameplay from the puzzle battles anyway, all you're after at this stage is the extra stimulation you earned.

So, to my surprise, I actually find myself recommending Mirror. It's not brilliant, but for the bargain price it goes for it's far better than expected and well worth getting (together with the DLC) if you like puzzle ero games. A bit of a hidden gem in the overflooded porn game genre.

The stories/gameplay for the first eight heroines in the game take around 35 to 40 minutes each for a total of around 296 minutes (Roughly around 5 hours of gameplay).
